basic_information.name: MinerU
basic_information.creator: OpenDataLab (Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
basic_information.description: MinerU is an open-source, high-precision document content extraction tool that transforms complex PDFs into LLM-ready Markdown and JSON for agentic workflows. It leverages a multi-model pipeline (LayoutLMv3, YOLOv8, UniMERNet, PaddleOCR) for layout detection, formula recognition (LaTeX), table extraction (HTML), and OCR across 84+ languages. MinerU2.5, a 1.2B-parameter decoupled VLM, surpasses GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro on the OmniDocBench benchmark while maintaining 2.12 pages/second throughput. It is widely adopted in RAG data preparation pipelines and academic document digitization.
basic_information.release_date: Initial open-source release: July 5, 2024. Public announcement: September 3, 2024. Stable v1.0.1: January 10, 2025. MinerU2.5 VLM model: September 2025. Latest release v2.7.6: February 6, 2026.
basic_information.license: AGPL-3.0 (future versions may explore more permissive licenses)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Multi-stage pipeline combining rule-based preprocessing/postprocessing with specialized AI models. The v1.x pipeline uses four sequential stages: (1) document preprocessing, (2) content parsing via PDF-Extract-Kit (layout detection, formula detection, table recognition, OCR), (3) content postprocessing, (4) format conversion to Markdown/JSON. MinerU2.5 introduces a decoupled two-stage VLM architecture: coarse layout analysis on downsampled images followed by targeted content recognition on native-resolution crops.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: N/A — MinerU is a document processing tool, not an embedding model. It produces structured text (Markdown, JSON, HTML tables, LaTeX formulas) that can be fed to any embedding model downstream.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — not a vector database. MinerU outputs structured documents for downstream indexing by other tools.
technical_architecture.scalability: Supports GPU (CUDA), NPU (CANN), and MPS acceleration, as well as CPU-only mode. Docker deployment available for containerized scaling. MinerU2.5 achieves 2.12 pages/second on a single A100 GPU with vLLM async engine. Layout detection runs at ~50ms per image on GPU. Without GPU, MinerU processes at ~3.3 sec/page on x86 CPU. With CUDA (Nvidia L4), it leads competitors at 0.21 sec/page.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted (pip/uv install, Docker), cloud web application at mineru.net (login required), Gradio-based online demos on HuggingFace Spaces and ModelScope, desktop client for Windows/Linux/macOS, API access via mineru.net.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: N/A — MinerU is a document processing/ingestion tool, not a retrieval engine. It prepares documents for downstream retrieval systems by converting PDFs to clean Markdown/JSON with preserved structure.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Document-structure-aware extraction: preserves headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and reading order. Outputs hierarchical structure that enables downstream semantic or structure-aware chunking. Removes headers, footers, footnotes, and page numbers to ensure semantic coherence. Supports single-column, multi-column, and complex layouts with human-readable reading order.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: N/A — not applicable to document processing tools. MinerU focuses on extraction quality rather than retrieval ranking.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Strong multimodal document processing: extracts images with captions, converts mathematical formulas to LaTeX, converts tables to HTML format, handles embedded charts and diagrams. MinerU2.5 uses a vision-language model for unified multimodal understanding. Supports scanned documents via OCR in 84+ languages (up to 109 with latest versions).
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No built-in knowledge graph construction. MinerU's structured output (headings, sections, cross-references) can feed into graph-based RAG systems like Microsoft GraphRAG or LightRAG for entity extraction and graph construction.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Preserves document structure including footnotes, table titles, image captions, and section headings, which enables downstream citation grounding. No built-in citation generation or grounding verification.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Produces clean, structured Markdown that removes non-semantic artifacts (headers, footers, page numbers), effectively reducing token waste in LLM context windows. The hierarchical structure output supports selective context loading by section or element type.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: With GPU (CUDA, Nvidia L4): 0.21 sec/page (fastest among open-source competitors). CPU-only (x86): ~3.3 sec/page. MinerU2.5 on A100: ~0.47 sec/page (2.12 pages/sec) with vLLM async engine. Layout detection: ~50ms per image on GPU.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: MinerU2.5: 2.12 pages/second on single A100 GPU (4x faster than MonkeyOCR-pro-3B). GPU-accelerated v1.x: ~4.76 pages/sec on Nvidia L4. CPU: ~0.3 pages/sec on x86.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: MinerU2.5 achieves 90.67 overall score on OmniDocBench (1,355 PDF pages, 9 document types, 4 layout types, 3 language types). Surpasses dots.ocr (88.41), MonkeyOCR-pro-3B (88.85), GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B across text recognition, formula recognition, table recognition, and reading order tasks.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: OmniDocBench (CVPR 2025): MinerU2.5 sets new state-of-the-art at 90.67, outperforming both general-purpose VLMs and domain-specific models. The benchmark covers comprehensive document parsing evaluation across diverse document types. MinerU v1.x dominates in generation and overall evaluation due to fine-grained local recognition based on layout detection results.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Dify: Official MinerU plugin available in Dify Marketplace (langgenius/mineru), supporting document parsing within Dify RAG workflows. n8n: Workflow template available for MinerU API + GPT-4o-mini document conversion. No official first-party LangChain or LlamaIndex document loader, but MinerU's Markdown/JSON output can be consumed by any framework's text loader. Third-party community integrations exist.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Model-agnostic output: produces Markdown and JSON that can be consumed by any LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, open-source). Internally uses specialized models: LayoutLMv3 (layout detection), YOLOv8/DocLayout-YOLO (formula detection), UniMERNet (formula recognition), TableMaster/StructEqTable (table recognition), PaddleOCR (text OCR). MinerU2.5 is a custom 1.2B VLM served via vLLM.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Community MCP server available (tinkpa/mcp-mineru on LobeHub), supporting PDF parsing with formula and table recognition through MCP protocol. Enables integration with Claude Desktop and other MCP-compatible LLM clients. Not an official first-party MCP server.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Primary input: PDF files (text-based and scanned). Also supports web pages and e-books. Accepts local files and URL links for batch processing via API. No native connectors to S3, databases, Confluence, etc. — designed as a focused document processing tool.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: No built-in observability or tracing integrations. When used within Dify workflows, inherits Dify's LangSmith/Langfuse observability. Standalone usage relies on application-level logging.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-source (AGPL-3.0) for self-hosted deployment — completely free. Cloud API available at mineru.net with login required — specific pricing tiers not publicly documented as of February 2026. Desktop client available for free download.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Self-hosted: fully free with no restrictions on usage volume. Cloud web version at mineru.net: free tier available (specific limits not publicly documented). HuggingFace Spaces demo: free for testing. Gradio WebUI: free, self-hosted.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Self-hosted cost is primarily compute: GPU recommended for production (A100 achieves 2.12 pages/sec, L4 achieves ~4.76 pages/sec). CPU-only is viable but ~15-20x slower. Cloud API pricing at mineru.net not publicly documented — contact OpenDataLab for enterprise quotes. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted: GPU cost (e.g., A100 at ~$1.50-2.00/hr cloud pricing) + storage for model weights (~2-5 GB) + compute for processing. At 2.12 pages/sec on A100, processing 100K pages costs approximately $13-17 in GPU time. CPU-only reduces hardware cost but increases processing time ~15x. AGPL license requires source disclosure if deployed as a network service, which may incur compliance costs for some enterprises. [uncertain]

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in open-source PDF document extraction. Ranked #1 among open-source PDF parsing tools in comparative evaluations. MinerU2.5 sets state-of-the-art on OmniDocBench, surpassing both commercial and open-source alternatives. Strong position in Chinese-language and multilingual document processing. 54K+ GitHub stars indicate very high community adoption.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Primarily adopted by the AI/ML research community, RAG pipeline developers, and data preparation teams for LLM training. Used extensively in academic document digitization workflows. Backed by Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, a major Chinese government-supported AI research institution. Specific named enterprise customers not publicly documented. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: ~54,100 stars, ~4,500 forks. PyPI package 'mineru' available for pip install. HuggingFace Space for online demo. Active GitHub Issues and Discussions (3,700+ discussions). Multiple community forks and integrations (Dify plugin, MCP server, n8n workflow, Docker images on Docker Hub).
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: OpenDataLab is a research division of the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (Shanghai AI Lab), a government-backed research institution inaugurated in September 2023. It operates within the Shanghai Foundation Model Innovation Center alongside Tencent, Alibaba, Microsoft, and SenseTime. Not a traditional VC-funded startup — funded through Chinese government and institutional research funding. No public valuation or funding round data.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Marker (PyMuPDF + Tesseract, GPL/commercial license, good structure fidelity), Docling (IBM, MIT license, modular and permissive), Unstructured.io (commercial + open-source, broad connector ecosystem), LlamaParse (LlamaIndex, cloud API), olmOCR (Allen AI). Key differentiators: (1) highest accuracy on OmniDocBench, (2) best multilingual OCR support (84-109 languages), (3) strong LaTeX formula and HTML table extraction, (4) GPU-accelerated speed leader (0.21 sec/page), (5) MinerU2.5 VLM achieves SOTA with only 1.2B parameters. Weakness: AGPL license is more restrictive than MIT (Docling) for commercial use.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Highly applicable for startups building RAG systems that need to ingest PDF-heavy document collections (legal, academic, financial, medical). Best suited for teams with some ML engineering capacity who can self-host. Ideal when: (1) documents contain complex elements like formulas, tables, or multi-column layouts, (2) multilingual support is needed (especially CJK languages), (3) high extraction accuracy is prioritized over ecosystem breadth. The AGPL license requires careful evaluation for commercial SaaS deployments — startups offering MinerU as part of a network service must open-source their code or obtain a commercial license.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Self-host (build): Free, full control, best for teams with GPU infrastructure and ML ops capability. Use Docker for quick setup. Ideal for startups processing sensitive documents that cannot leave their infrastructure. Buy (mineru.net API): Simpler setup, no GPU management, but vendor dependency on OpenDataLab's cloud service. Alternative: Consider Docling (MIT license, easier commercial use) if AGPL compliance is a concern, or Unstructured.io if broader connector ecosystem is needed.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: Quick start: 30 minutes to first extraction via pip install + CLI. Docker deployment: 1-2 hours. Production pipeline with GPU optimization: 1-2 weeks. Integration into full RAG pipeline (with chunking, embedding, vector DB): 2-4 weeks. Dify plugin integration: hours.
key_lessons: Document extraction quality directly determines RAG answer quality — garbage in, garbage out. MinerU's state-of-the-art accuracy on OmniDocBench means fewer hallucinations and better retrieval downstream.

AGPL license is a double-edged sword: it ensures the tool stays open-source but creates compliance obligations for SaaS startups. Evaluate early whether your business model is compatible, and consider Docling (MIT) as an alternative if not.
GPU acceleration provides 15-20x speedup over CPU — budget for GPU infrastructure if processing more than a few hundred pages daily. A single A100 can process ~7,600 pages/hour.

MinerU excels at multilingual and scientific documents (formulas, tables), making it the clear choice for academic, legal, and technical document processing. For simple English text-only PDFs, lighter tools like Marker may suffice.

The Dify plugin and MCP server integrations show a trend toward document processing tools becoming composable building blocks in AI agent workflows — consider how your document pipeline fits into the broader agentic architecture.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — MinerU offers a web GUI at mineru.net (zero-install, login required), a desktop client for Windows/Linux/macOS, and a Gradio-based WebUI for self-hosted no-code usage. The Dify plugin also provides a no-code workflow integration.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy for document processing tools in RAG pipelines), Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — using MinerU's no-code interface for document extraction)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official GitHub repository (54K+ stars), two published arXiv papers (2409.18839 and 2509.22186), OmniDocBench benchmark (CVPR 2025), and multiple independent comparative evaluations.
confidence.cross_reference: Architecture and features confirmed across GitHub README, arXiv paper, PyPI listing, official documentation site, and independent blog comparisons (Jimmy Song, liduos.com, tyolab.com). Benchmark results confirmed by OmniDocBench CVPR 2025 paper and neurohive.io analysis.
confidence.caveats: AGPL-3.0 license creates significant restrictions for commercial SaaS use — enterprises must evaluate compliance carefully. The 84-language OCR claim is from initial release; latest versions claim up to 109 languages. MinerU2.5 (the VLM model) is a separate model from the v1.x pipeline approach — features and performance differ between versions. OpenDataLab's cloud API pricing is not publicly transparent. The project is evolving rapidly (v2.7.6 as of Feb 2026), so specific numbers may change quickly.
confidence.security_posture: AGPL license means source code must be disclosed if deployed as a network service. PDF processing carries inherent risks (malicious PDFs, embedded scripts) — MinerU does not document specific security hardening measures. Model weights are downloaded from external sources (HuggingFace, ModelScope) — standard supply chain trust considerations apply. No documented SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other compliance certifications. For enterprise use, self-hosted deployment behind firewalls is recommended for sensitive documents.
